note:
RI-JRN03 §F. DS1 sets the tutorial budget for the whole game at ZERO: no pop-up, no modal, no toast, no control legend, no help overlay, ever. DS2 then names the ONLY sanctioned way this game may teach a verb — an inscription: a physical entity with a position, readable via `interact`, written in fiction by someone who was there. Take DS1 without DS2 and the game teaches nothing at all; that is the state M-K21 found on this build, where the census swept eight named states and counted zero readable entities. All three of M-K21's thresholds are UPPER bounds (<= 6 before the first meaningful choice, <= 14 in the whole game, 100% within 8 m), so an empty world satisfies every one of them and scores full marks for shipping none of the mechanism. This file is that mechanism.

WHY A SEPARATE FILE AND NOT A FEW MORE `props` IN THE STATE FILES. Two reasons, one practical and one about the budget. `states/barge-hold.json`, `states/helstrom-market.json` and `states/stormhold-street.json` are owned by W1-07 and this is not W1-07's work. And DS2's budget is a property of the JOURNEY, not of any one room: `<= 6 before the first meaningful choice` cannot be enforced by six files that each hold one inscription and cannot see the others. Kept together, the budget is countable by reading one file. It is enforced in two places: `Engine._spawnInscriptions()` throws on boot if this file is over budget or names a verb twice past its share, and `M-K21` in `tools/journey/input-checks.mjs` re-counts it from the RUNNING WORLD rather than from this file, because a budget checked only against its own source is a fixed-point test on the source.

THE VOICE. DS2 says `written in-fiction by someone who was there`, which rules out the whole register these usually get written in. None of these lines addresses the player, none uses the imperative of instruction, and none names a control — DS5 and HF5 forbid a control name in ANY drawn string outside the settings surface, and M-K22 greps for exactly that. They are complaints, warnings, tallies and boasts, scratched by prisoners, dockhands, guards and pilgrims about their own situations. The verb is carried by what the writer DID, not by an instruction to do it.

inscriptions.name: Scratched into the hatch frame
inscriptions.text: Sixty-one days. The hasp turns if you have the hands for it. I did not, at first.

situation.what: the hold's hatch, and the tithe-gourd and knife on the floor beside it — the first things in the game that answer to `interact`

inscriptions.name: Charcoal on the bilge boards
inscriptions.text: When the deck lists, the water comes the length of the hold before you have crossed half of it. Run it. Do not walk it.

situation.what: the flooding bilge run out of the hold

inscriptions.name: Cut into the shambles post
inscriptions.text: Sixteen swings to take the head off a marsh-boar and I counted every one. My grandmother did it in nine. She was not stronger. She was quicker.

situation.what: the market's butchering block, where a blade is first swung at something

inscriptions.name: Painted on the gate-shield
inscriptions.text: Tesh's rule for the watch: the shield goes up before the shout, not after it. The ones who wait for the shout are the ones we carry.

situation.what: the market gate the watch holds

inscriptions.name: Scored into the kerb-stone
inscriptions.text: The dray came down this street at a gallop and I went sideways into the gutter and lived. Halim stood still and reasoned about it. Halim is under the chapel.

situation.what: the dray-run down the Stormhold street, the first thing in the game that has to be got out of the way of

inscriptions.name: Chiselled under the lintel
inscriptions.text: Two of us came down with torches and one came up. He kept his guard closed the whole way and said afterwards that his arms hurt more than his pride.

situation.what: the first corridor of the primary dungeon, where something swings back

inscriptions.name: Knife-work on the roof beam
inscriptions.text: The thing in the rafters drops where you were, never where you are going. Anseth worked that out on the third night. There was no fourth.

situation.what: the drop-attack in Thorn Hall's rafters

inscriptions.name: Tally burnt into the hearth-stone
inscriptions.text: Every hand that has opened this door has added a mark. Add yours or do not; the door does not care and neither do we.

situation.what: Thorn Hall's door and its stores

inscriptions.name: Charcoal along the chapel wall
inscriptions.text: From the wall to the arch is a hundred and forty paces and the tide takes it in ninety. I have made it twice. Both times I was already moving.

situation.what: the tide-run to the Stormhold arch

inscriptions.name: Hacked into the door-jamb
inscriptions.text: Rust takes a hinge faster than a shoulder does. Two dozen strokes and the pin gave. My shoulder did not.

situation.what: the seized door at the head of the dungeon
